## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to translate security requirements into a enforceable policy and CI flow for a multi-tenant cluster. It also evaluates practical policy testing across PRs.

## Key Concepts

- Kyverno ClusterPolicy for container securityContext checks
- Kubernetes pod/spec validation in Deployments/StatefulSets
- CI gate integration with PR workflows
- Test manifests to verify both compliant and non-compliant cases

## Code Example

```javascript
// Kyverno policy (as YAML in practice)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-privileged-containers
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-secctx
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Job"]
    validate:
      message: "Container must drop ALL capabilities, run as non-root, and readOnly rootfs"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop:
                    - ALL
```

- How to test locally with sample manifests?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assess mastery of reproducible builds, attestation, SBOMs, and supply chain controls in CI/CD for a multi-service repo.

## Key Concepts

- Reproducible builds, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
- Image signing with cosign and attestation
- SBOM generation with Syft and verification against digest
- Monorepo with multiple languages and per-service artifacts

## Code Example

```yaml
name: Repro Build Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build deterministically
        run: |
          export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct HEAD)
          docker buildx build --build-arg SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --tag $IMAGE .
      - name: Sign image
        run: cosign sign $IMAGE
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: syft packages docker://${IMAGE} -o spdx
      - name: Verify
        run: cosign verify --signature public.key --certificate-identity-id "monorepo" $IMAGE
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate cosign keys and SBOM verification keys?
- How do you handle caching and parallelization in a large mono-repo?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes policy-as-code skills, Istio security posture, and CI/CD integration. It tests ability to craft minimal, verifiable manifests and to reason about runtime vs CI checks.

## Key Concepts

- Istio PeerAuthentication mtls: STRICT
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno policy or alternative
- CI validation: lint, dry-run apply, policy testing
- Runtime enforcement: Istio sidecars enforce mTLS

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8smtlstrict
spec:
  crd:
    Spec:
      groups: ["constraints.gatekeeper.sh"]
      names:
        kind: K8sMTLSStrict
        plural: k8smTLSStricts
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8smtlstrict
        violation["mtls_missing"] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Namespace"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["istio-injection"]
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sMTLSStrict
metadata:
  name: mtls-strict
spec:
  match:
    requiredImages: []
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest: PeerAuthentication with mtls: STRICT
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: default
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest: missing PeerAuthentication
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample
  namespace: test
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you enable gradual rollout for mTLS enforcement?
- What exceptions would you permit and how would you audit them?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement real-world security gates that combine image scanning, attestation, and policy enforcement in a scalable multi‑tenant environment.

## Key Concepts

- Admission control with OPA/Kyverno
- SBOMs and CVE scoring via Trivy
- Image signing with cosign and Rekor attestation
- PR‑level gating and local verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: scan SBOM, sign, and publish attestation
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Run Trivy SBOM
    run: trivy image --format cyclonedx -o sbom.json image:tag
  - name: Cosign sign SBOM
    run: cosign sign -key cosign.pub sbom.json
  - name: Rekor attestation
    run: cosign attest sbom.json --type sbom --format json
```

```yaml
# OPA policy (partial) enforcing CVE threshold and SBOM signing
package gate
default allow = false
allow {
  input.images[_].cve_score <= 6.0
  input.images[_].sbom_signed
}
```

```yaml
# Minimal manifest examples (one failing, one passing)
# failing: image with high CVE score
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-fail
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example/unsafe:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# passing: compliant image
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example/secure:1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

## Follow-up Questions

- What thresholds would you adjust for prod vs. staging?
- How would you scale the gate across many clusters and tenants?

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests foundational secure supply chain practices in a beginner-friendly manner. It mirrors real-world CI gates used in production environments around Dockerfile hygiene, image signing, SBOM generation, and registry controls. It introduces modern tools like Cosign and SBOM attestations without overwhelming complexity.

## Key Concepts

- **Dockerfile Hygiene**: Non-root USER and multi-stage builds reduce security vulnerabilities and image size
- **Container Image Signing**: Using Cosign to sign and verify container images ensures integrity
- **SBOM Attestation**: Software Bill of Materials provides transparency into image contents and dependencies
- **GitHub Actions Workflows**: Implementing gates and policy checks in CI/CD pipelines
- **Registry Allowlist**: Restricting deployments to approved registries prevents supply chain attacks

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Docker Security Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Validate Dockerfile
        run: |
          # Check for non-root USER
          grep -q 'USER ' Dockerfile || exit 1
          # Check for multi-stage build
          grep -q 'FROM.*AS' Dockerfile || exit 1
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json > sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign image and SBOM with Cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
          cosign attest --type spdx-json --predicate sbom.json ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Verify signature and attestation
        run: |
          cosign verify ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
```

- Kubernetes RBAC and ServiceAccounts
- Pod security: RunAsNonRoot, ReadOnlyRootFilesystem, imagePullPolicy
- CI gate integration and drift checks

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal ConstraintTemplate example
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8stenant
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sTenantConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8stenant
      # ... policy rules ...
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test policy in CI for both passing and failing manifests?
- How would you handle policy versioning and breaking changes in production?

questions.explanation:
This question evaluates end-to-end security across CI, admission control, and runtime enforcement in a multi-cloud, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It assesses understanding of image provenance, SBOM handling, and runtime integrity enforcement.

Key concepts tested include:
- Sigstore Cosign attestations and keyless verification workflows
- SBOM generation with Syft and SPDX/CycloneDX formats
- Digest pinning to prevent tag-based supply chain attacks
- OPA/Kyverno policy engine configuration and validation patterns
- Kubernetes security contexts (readOnlyRootFilesystem, runAsNonRoot, seccompProfile)
- Pod Security Standards and namespace-level enforcement
- Multi-tenant isolation and least-privilege container execution
